cards.front: Name the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
cards.back: **Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.** Sustainability was the sixth, added in 2021.

cards.front: List the six general design principles of the Well-Architected Framework.
cards.back: Stop guessing capacity needs; test at production scale; automate with experimentation in mind; consider evolutionary architectures; drive architectures using data; improve through **game days**.
cards.updated: Two principles are now titled 'Automate with architectural experimentation in mind' and 'Consider evolutionary architectures'.

cards.front: What is a game day in Well-Architected terms?
cards.back: A scheduled exercise that simulates a production event (an outage, a flash sale, a security incident) to see how the architecture and the team cope, and to find improvements before it happens for real.

cards.front: Which pillar does 'replace one large resource with several small ones to reduce the impact of a single failure' belong to?
cards.back: **Reliability**: the design principle *scale horizontally to increase aggregate workload availability*.

cards.front: Name four reliability design principles.
cards.back: Automatically recover from failure; test recovery procedures; scale horizontally to increase aggregate availability; stop guessing capacity; manage change through automation (any four).

cards.front: Which security design principle says to reduce or eliminate direct human access to data?
cards.back: **Keep people away from data**: use tools and automation instead of manual access, to cut mishandling, modification and human error.

cards.front: What does the security principle 'implement a strong identity foundation' ask for?
cards.back: Least privilege, separation of duties, centralised identity management and no reliance on long-term static credentials (use roles and temporary credentials).

cards.front: Operational excellence: why prefer frequent, small, reversible changes?
cards.back: Small automated changes have a small blast radius and can be rolled back quickly when something fails, so teams can ship often without risking big outages.

cards.front: Name three performance efficiency design principles.
cards.back: Democratize advanced technologies (consume them as services); go global in minutes; use serverless architectures; experiment more often; consider mechanical sympathy (any three).

cards.front: Cost optimization: what saving does AWS quote for stopping dev/test environments outside working hours?
cards.back: About **75 %**: running 40 hours a week (8 hours x 5 days) instead of 168. It illustrates the *adopt a consumption model* principle.

cards.front: Sustainability: why is one host at 60 % utilization better than two hosts at 30 %?
cards.back: Every host has a baseline power draw, so consolidating work onto fewer, busier hosts uses less energy. This is the *maximize utilization* principle.

cards.front: How is responsibility for sustainability split between AWS and the customer?
cards.back: AWS: sustainability **of** the cloud (efficient infrastructure, renewable energy, water). Customer: sustainability **in** the cloud (right-sizing, utilization, deleting idle resources, efficient storage and code).

cards.front: Do you make trade-offs between Well-Architected pillars?
cards.back: Yes, based on business context (for example less redundancy in dev to save cost, extra cost for mission-critical reliability). **Security and operational excellence are generally not traded off.**
cards.updated: The slides call the pillars a synergy, not trade-offs; the current framework text describes trade-offs.

cards.front: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool and what does it cost?
cards.back: A free console service for reviewing a **workload** against the framework: you answer questions per pillar and get high and medium risks, an improvement plan, reports and milestones. You pay only for your own resources.

cards.front: In the Well-Architected Tool, what are HRIs and MRIs?
cards.back: **High risk issues**: choices AWS has found can significantly hurt the business. **Medium risk issues**: choices that hurt it to a lesser extent. They feed the improvement plan.

cards.front: What is a milestone in the Well-Architected Tool?
cards.back: An immutable snapshot of a workload's review at a point in time. Save one after the first full review and after each round of improvements to show progress.

cards.front: What is a lens in the Well-Architected Tool?
cards.back: An extra set of questions and best practices for a workload type or industry (Serverless, SaaS, Generative AI, Machine Learning, IoT and more). The Framework lens is applied automatically; you can add official or custom lenses (up to 20 per workload).

cards.front: What are the six AWS Trusted Advisor check categories?
cards.back: Cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits (quotas) and operational excellence.

cards.front: Which Trusted Advisor checks do Basic Support accounts get?
cards.back: All **service limits** checks plus a core set: EBS public snapshots, RDS public snapshots, S3 bucket permissions, MFA on root account, security groups with specific ports unrestricted, and STS global endpoint usage. Refresh is manual.
cards.updated: Current core list per the Trusted Advisor check reference (2026).

cards.front: Which support plans unlock the full Trusted Advisor check set and API access?
cards.back: **Business Support+, Enterprise Support or Unified Operations.** Basic (and the retiring Developer plan) get only the core checks and no Trusted Advisor or Support API.
cards.updated: Business Support+ and Unified Operations are new plans; Developer, Business and Enterprise On-Ramp end on 1 January 2027.

cards.front: You want an alert when a Trusted Advisor check turns red. What do you build, and where?
cards.back: An **EventBridge rule in us-east-1** (Trusted Advisor is global and emits its events there) targeting SNS or Lambda. Requires Business Support+ or higher.

cards.front: When does a Trusted Advisor service limits check turn yellow and red?
cards.back: **Yellow at 80 %** of the limit, **red at 100 %**. Request increases through Service Quotas (or a support case if Service Quotas does not cover the service).

cards.front: Trusted Advisor vs Well-Architected Tool: which one scans your account automatically?
cards.back: **Trusted Advisor** scans resources and configuration automatically. The Well-Architected Tool is a guided questionnaire answered by people (it can display Trusted Advisor data if you activate the integration).

cards.front: SAA-C03 format: questions, time, scored items and pass mark?
cards.back: **65 questions** (50 scored, 15 unscored) in **130 minutes**; scaled score 100-1,000; **720** to pass; compensatory scoring (overall score only). Fee USD 150.

cards.front: SAA-C03 domains and their weights?
cards.back: Design Secure Architectures **30 %**, Design Resilient Architectures **26 %**, Design High-Performing Architectures **24 %**, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures **20 %**.

cards.front: After the exam: when do results arrive, how long to wait before a retake, how long is the certification valid?
cards.back: Results within **5 business days**; retake after **14 calendar days**; certification valid **3 years**.
cards.updated: AWS now states 5 business days for results.

cards.front: Is there a penalty for guessing on AWS certification exams?
cards.back: No. Unanswered questions are scored as wrong, so always pick an answer, flag it and come back if time allows.

cards.front: Exam strategy: two options both work. How do you choose?
cards.back: Re-read the qualifier (most cost-effective, least operational overhead, most secure, highly available). The option that meets **every** requirement with the simplest managed design usually wins; complex custom builds are typical distractors.

cards.front: Which AWS whitepapers are worth skimming before SAA-C03?
cards.back: The **AWS Well-Architected Framework** (and pillar papers) and **Disaster Recovery of Workloads on AWS**. The older 'Architecting for the Cloud: AWS Best Practices' paper is archived.
cards.updated: 'Architecting for the Cloud' (October 2018) is archived and points to the Well-Architected Framework.

cards.front: Where do you find vetted, deployable reference architectures beyond this course?
cards.back: The **AWS Architecture Center** (diagrams, decision guides, whitepapers) and the **AWS Solutions Library** (AWS Solutions with code, Guidance, partner solutions).
